requirements.statement: FS0 Governance SHALL implement Design Proposal -> Design -> Plan -> Build -> accepted repository state.
Design SHALL use Audit, Normalize, Accept; Plan SHALL use Analyze, Specify, Accept; Build SHALL use Implement, Verify, Accept.

Each governed Design, Plan, and Build work item SHALL record stable identity, predecessor, scope, material exclusions where applicable, candidate result, completion conditions, disposition, provenance, and bounded_authorization containing acceptance_actor.
Design SHALL consume a non-authoritative Design Proposal.
Plan SHALL consume accepted Design authority and define realization intent covering affected artifacts, Conformance work, Assurance work, dependencies, sequencing, and bounded Build scope.
Build SHALL consume an accepted Plan and implement only work authorized by that Plan.
Semantic defects SHALL route to Design, realization-intent defects to Plan, and implementation defects to Build.
Governance acceptance SHALL be explicit, attributable, traceable, candidate-specific, and realized by an authorized merge of an eligible governed pull request.
A Governance acceptance decision SHALL depend only on authority accepted before the candidate acquires authority produced by that acceptance.
A governed work item SHALL authorize only its explicit scope.
Each governed pull request SHALL identify exactly one governed-work issue; one governed-work issue MAY be realized through one or more pull requests.
A governed pull request MAY contain one or more commits; acceptance applies to the complete current pull-request candidate change set.
Required Conformance and Assurance SHALL gate merge eligibility for the complete current governed pull-request candidate.
Bootstrap acceptance SHALL be the authorized merge of the designated bootstrap-cutover pull request after passing bootstrap mechanical validation.
A merge candidate SHALL retain the exact accepted predecessor identities it depends on and SHALL be reevaluated if an applicable predecessor changes.
After cutover, refs/heads/main SHALL identify the accepted repository state resulting from the most recent authorized governed pull-request merge.
Closing, approval, workflow success, Conformance success, or Assurance findings SHALL NOT independently create acceptance; authorized merge of an eligible governed PR SHALL.
Initial bootstrap SHALL use one dedicated provenance issue and one designated bootstrap-cutover pull request targeting refs/heads/main.
For governed merge acceptance, the GitHub merge actor SHALL equal the governed issue bounded_authorization.acceptance_actor.
After FS0 cutover, every persistent framework change SHALL occur through FS0 Governance.
